    Warren Buffett Stated Stocks Are Better Than Bonds for Long-Term Investors. History Demonstrates He Was Right.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1070 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF ›.
    • According to recent reports, warren Buffett became a legendary investor by investing in stocks, not bonds.
    • Recent findings suggest that many people think of bonds as being "less risky" than stocks, and that can be true.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Ben Gran – Nov 21, 2026 at 12:45PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF ›.

    According to recent reports, warren Buffett became a legendary investor by investing in stocks, not bonds. But he had some strong opinions about bonds that other investors should consider.

    Recent findings suggest that many people think of bonds as being "less risky" than stocks, and that can be true. But understanding the "risk" of bonds vs. stocks depends on your time horizon and investment goals.

    In his 2017 shareholder letter to Berkshire Hathaway shareholders, Warren Buffett shared an interesting story about his experience with the true risks of bonds. This experience reminded him why he prefers buying stocks.

    Let's look at why Buffett mentioned that stocks are a better buy than bonds for most long-term investors.

    In 2017, Buffett was reaching the end of a unique, public 10-year-long wager. He had made a friendly bet with an investment advisory firm, Protégé Partners, to see if professional hedge fund managers could outperform the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) for the next 10 years, starting in 2008.

    Buffett bet that they couldn't. He believed that most professional money managers would fail to beat the S&P 500 for that long.

    Sources indicate that buffett was right. All five of the professional hedge fund managers chosen by Protégé failed to beat the S&P 500.

    The bet involved $1 million, with Buffett and Protégé each pledging $500,000 toward that total. No matter who won the bet, the $1 million proceeds would go to a Nebraska charity, Girls Inc. of Omaha.

    Recent findings suggest that to fund the bet, Buffett and Protégé each bought a package of zero-coupon U.S. Treasury bonds worth $318,250 when purchased at the start of the bet (about 64% of face value) and would be worth $500,000 after 10 years (for a total of $1 million at the end of the bet).

    Industry observers note that but midway through the bet, in 2012, Buffett realized that due to recent changes in the bond market, their zero-coupon Treasury bonds had become a terrible investment. The bonds had started out yielding about 4.56% annually, but by 2012, with five years left until maturity, they were yielding only about 0.88% annually.

    Warren Buffett can't abide a bad deal on an investment. He and Protégé rapidly agreed to sell their Treasury bonds and put the proceeds into Berkshire Hathaway (BRKB -0.36%) Class B shares. He was confident that Berkshire Hathaway stock would deliver a much better average annual return for the next five years than 0.88%.

    Once again, he was right. As a result, as Buffett wrote: "Girls Inc. of Omaha found itself receiving $2,222,279 last month rather than the $1 million it had originally hoped for.".

    Buffett's experience with Treasury bonds taught a few key lessons about the real risks of bond investing. Here are a few reasons, according to Buffett, why bonds can be riskier than stocks:.

    Buffett wrote that investing is about giving up consumption today so you can have more money to spend later. But bonds can fail to achieve this goal if they don't make your money grow in the long run.

    As he wrote, "By that standard, purportedly 'risk-free' long-term bonds in 2012 were a far riskier investment than a long-term investment in common stocks.".

    If inflation is 3% per year and bonds deliver 4% yields, they're barely staying ahead of inflation. Buffett bought those zero-coupon Treasury bonds at a time of lower inflation and lower interest rates than we have today. But from 2012 to 2017, his bonds were on track to yield only 0.88% per year.

    Buffett noted this inflation risk of bonds when he wrote: "At that time, even a 1% annual rate of inflation between 2012 and 2017 would have decreased the purchasing-power of the government bond that Protégé and I sold.".

    The S&P 500 can crash on any given day, but it tends to go up in the long run. That means the longer your time horizon, the longer you can hold your stocks, and the more likely they’ll deliver a positive return. Bonds can be safer than stocks in the short run, but over time, stocks gradually become a better bet.

    As Buffett wrote: "...in any upcoming day, week, or even year, stocks will be riskier -- far riskier -- than short-term U.S. bonds. As an investor's investment horizon lengthens, however, a diversified portfolio of U.S. equities becomes progressively less risky than bonds, assuming that the stocks are purchased at a sensible multiple of earnings relative to then-prevailing interest rates.".

    According to recent reports, buffett followed up on these ideas in his shareholder letter in a February 2018 interview with CNBC, where he mentioned he believed long-term investors should buy stocks rather than bonds. He said, "If you had to choose between buying long-term bonds or equities, I would choose equities in a minute...If I were going to own a 30-year government bond or own equities for 30 years, I think equities will considerably outperform that 30-year bond.".

    History indicates that Warren Buffett was right. In the eight years since Buffett's shareholder letter and CNBC interview in Feb. 2018, the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -3.42%) has strongly outperformed the Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF (BND +0.59%).

    BND Total Return Level data by YCharts.

    This doesn't mean you shouldn't buy any bonds. Bond ETFs can be appropriate as part of a diversified portfolio. Today's bonds offer higher yields than they did when Buffett was buying Treasury bonds in 2008, which could make them a better deal for investors than they used to be. I own shares of the Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF, even though my time horizon for investing is still decades long.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    But if you want maximum growth of your money and can hold for the long term through short-term stock market booms and busts, buying stocks should be the foundation of your investment strategy.

    Airbnb’s Latest $12 Billion Buyback Is Backed by a 35% Free Cash Flow Margin. Here’s What It Means for Shareholders.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (754 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, airbnb (ABNB -1.41%) has historically posted strong growth metrics.
    • Recent findings suggest that momentum is picking up.
    • Industry observers note that besides the growth story, investors shouldn't overlook Airbnb's impressive profitability.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Neil Patel – Nov 21, 2026 at 12:55PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Airbnb ›.

    In a recent development, airbnb (ABNB -1.41%) has historically posted strong growth metrics. This is usually what happens when businesses disrupt massive industries and rapidly steal market share.

    Recent findings suggest that momentum is picking up. During the third quarter (ended Sept. 30), the organization reported a year-over-year revenue gain of 19%, beating analyst estimates. Gross booking value climbed 21%.

    Industry observers note that besides the growth story, investors shouldn't overlook Airbnb's impressive profitability. Trailing-12-month free cash flow (FCF) of $4.9 billion accounted for 35% of revenue, which is a superb margin. The board of directors had the confidence to approve a $12 billion buyback, in addition to the $2.7 billion in existing capacity.

    Recent findings suggest that the growth stock has had a wonderful year. It's up 33% in 2026 (as of Nov. 18). Here's what that share repurchase runway means for investors.

    According to recent reports, airbnb is known for having sizable stock-based compensation, totaling $1.4 billion over the last nine months. This is how businesses, particularly those earlier in their life cycles, pay their employees. But it results in an increase in the share count.

    Industry observers note that to Airbnb's credit, though, its outstanding share count shrank by almost 3% in the past year. The manufacturer conducted $4 billion in stock buybacks over the last 12 months. Combining the new $12 billion repurchase authorization with the $2.7 billion remaining capacity means Airbnb now intends to buy 12% of the company's entire market capitalization.

    Investors benefit from this tailwind. A smaller outstanding share count provides a jolt to earnings per share (EPS). Shareholders who continue to hold the stock see their ownership percentage in the business increase over time.

    The best companies can balance returning capital to investors with reinvesting into their operations. Airbnb is certainly still playing offense.

    In a recent development, the business continues to expand its list of services. Travelers can now book hotels. And there are more active partnerships in place. And for hosts, a redesigned calendar makes juggling multiple listings far simpler.

    Airbnb is also leaning into the opportunity that artificial intelligence (AI) presents. It plans to release an AI-powered travel assistant in 2027.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that for context, in fiscal 2026 (ended Sept. 26), Apple (AAPL -1.90%) produced $136.1 billion in FCF, a mind-boggling figure. Its FCF margin was 28%, however, which is lower than Airbnb’s FCF margin.

    Recent findings suggest that hats off to Airbnb's asset-light business model. The firm doesn't own the properties listed on its platform, eliminating the need for a sizable investment. And that frees up cash for repurchasing shares.

    This leads to the next point, which concerns the wide economic moat Airbnb has built since its founding in 2007. The firm benefits from a powerful global network effect. It's a positive feedback loop in which more guest bookings attract more hosts to try to make money from their listings. In turn, the wider selection leads to a better, more compelling experience for travelers.

    The fear that AI agents will handle the entire booking process for consumers and challenge this favorable position is warranted. However, Airbnb's advantage as the middleman comes from convenience, trust, and centralized tools it offers to both guests and hosts. The strong Q3 financial figures prove there is no cause for alarm yet.

    "As we build Airbnb to become an AI-native company, I actually think the opportunity ahead of us is actually even bigger," co-founder and chief executive officer Brian Chesky said on the Q3 2026 earnings call.

    Airbnb is worth keeping an eye on, provided you're an investor searching for high-quality stocks to own for five years or more. It's a compounding machine. Consensus analyst estimates call for EPS to grow at an annualized rate of 24% from fiscal 2025 to fiscal 2028.

    According to recent reports, because shares trade at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 29.7, much of the good news is already reflected. Know this before you make a move.

    If the Fed Hikes Rates This Year, I'm Loading Up on This 1 ETF

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (708 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Energy ETF ›.
    • With just three weeks left before the Federal Reserve's December meeting, it's basically a foregone conclusion that the central bank will raise interest rates for a second time this year.
    • Speaking of interest rates, investors preparing for 2027 should note that Goldman Sachs recently forecast one more rate hike by the Fed next March, before the central bank begins to cut rates later in the year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Todd Shriber – Nov 21, 2026 at 1:08PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Vanguard Energy ETF ›.

    With just three weeks left before the Federal Reserve's December meeting, it's basically a foregone conclusion that the central bank will raise interest rates for a second time this year.

    Speaking of interest rates, investors preparing for 2027 should note that Goldman Sachs recently forecast one more rate hike by the Fed next March, before the central bank begins to cut rates later in the year. We don’t know what the future holds, but the point is, it's nearly a sure thing that at least one more rate increase is on the way and more can't be ruled out.

    Sources indicate that federal Reserve headquarters in Washington, D.C. Image source: Getty Images.

    It has been revealed that so now is an excellent time for equity investors of all stripes to understand that Fed actions affect various sectors in different ways. For example, the capital-intensive, debt-heavy utility sector is often vulnerable to higher borrowing costs when rates rise. In contrast, higher rates are seen as boons to financial services stocks due to net interest margin expansion.

    Energy stocks have also shown strength as rates rise, suggesting that exchange-traded funds (ETFs) such as the Vanguard Energy ETF (VDE -0.73%) are worth considering ahead of the next Fed meeting and beyond.

    Home to the largest domestic energy companies, the $11.9 billion Vanguard Energy ETF is one of this year's stars among basic sector ETFs, as highlighted by a year-to-date gain of 43% as I write this.

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that there's no denying that energy ETFs, including this Vanguard fund, are getting big boosts from oil prices driven up by current wars, but energy stocks also have a track record of performing well when interest rates rise. The Fed — whose main role is to promote “maximum employment” and “stable prices” — has already raised rates once this year, and 10- and 30-year Treasury yields recently touched their highest levels since 2002.

    The bottom line is that energy stocks and ETFs such as this Vanguard fund are doing their jobs in a challenging interest rate environment, providing investors with effective portfolio hedges while stocks and bonds falter.

    So it's pretty safe to say that we're in for at least one more rate hike, if not two, in the short term, but that doesn't make this Vanguard ETF a risk-free bet heading into 2027. Oil prices are notoriously volatile, and if latest Democratic majorities in both houses of Congress succeed in compelling President Donald Trump to end the war in Iran, oil prices would likely tumble, potentially taking energy ETFs along for the ride.

    According to recent reports, additionally, this ETF is top-heavy. It allocates nearly 40% of its weight to ExxonMobil (XOM +0.67%) and Chevron (CVX +0.91%). Those stocks have been sturdy this year, but if one sneezes, it's possible, if not probable, the other does the same, and this Vanguard ETF catches a cold.

    Of course, there are no guarantees that any of those scenarios come to pass. I'm just laying out possible risks for investors evaluating this ETF.

    In a recent development, there are plenty of bright spots to ponder, too. For example, Exxon and Chevron have strong balance sheets and are two of the energy patch's most dependable dividend growers. And in broader terms, the global energy sector is sporting the best earnings momentum of any sector over the past several months. On that basis, energy is even beating technology, and by a healthy margin at that.     💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that november has been absolutely terrible for Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%).
    • This is all happening against the backdrop of a generative artificial intelligence (AI) industry that many fear could be a bubble that is soon to be popped by changing regulation and investor appetite for risk.
    • Nvidia's current crisis began on Oct.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Will Ebiefung – Nov 21, 2026 at 1:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Recent findings suggest that november has been absolutely terrible for Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%). A series of scandals has led to the removal of its CEO and founder, Jensen Huang. Widespread uncertainty about the company's future has caused shares to drop nearly 30% since the start of the month.

    This is all happening against the backdrop of a generative artificial intelligence (AI) industry that many fear could be a bubble that is soon to be popped by changing regulation and investor appetite for risk. Let's dig deeper into the pros and cons of Nvidia to decide what might come next.

    Nvidia's current crisis began on Oct. 29, when The Fresh York Times reported that its CEO, Jensen Huang, was a possible target of an espionage plot. The suspicions centered around his relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at one of Nvidia's major clients, the Singapore-based Megaspeed. Jensen Huang was also involved in potential misconduct related to his relationships with Nvidia employees. On Nov. 12, he resigned amid a board investigation expected to lead to his termination.

    In a recent development, these developments led to a sharp decline in Nvidia's stock price, and it isn't hard to see why. For starters, the espionage allegations will cast a dark shadow over Nvidia's entire Asian operation. Buyers in countries like Singapore and Malaysia could be used to reroute Nvidia's most advanced chips to China, bypassing U.S. sanctions.

    In a recent development, there may even be unwanted regulatory scrutiny of Nvidia's past business dealings with China-affiliated clients. Huang is expected to eventually testify before U.S. lawmakers concerning this glitch.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    In a recent development, however, beyond the tangible business effects, Nvidia may now face an even bigger problem: the loss of its founder's vision. Huang's leadership was instrumental in helping turn Nvidia from just another Silicon Valley hardware producer into the world's largest chipmaker. It is unclear if a latest CEO will have the same vision and tenacity. According to Dan Ives, an analyst at Yorkville Ives, the tech giant could lose up to 30% of its value without Huang at the helm. That's bad news for investors.

    The good news is that Nvidia's chip business is still firing on all cylinders. Third-quarter earnings were a slam dunk, with revenue jumping 103% year over year to $115.8 billion. This result was driven by ravenous demand from data center clients, which use Nvidia's hardware to run and train large language models (LLMs) and other AI-related use cases.

    Jensen Huang. Image source: Nvidia.

    The soaring growth is expected to continue over the next few quarters, as AI-related spending reveals no sign of slowing any time soon. S&P Global expects America's largest hyperscalers to spend $1.3 trillion on AI infrastructure next year. Much of that capital will likely flow into Nvidia's products because of their cutting-edge design and capabilities.

    That said, Nvidia's data center segment now represents 93% of its revenue, making the organization exceptionally vulnerable to a drop in data center demand.

    According to recent reports, the market could weaken because of regulatory changes. Many Democratic lawmakers are already pledging to push back on data center construction. Rising interest rates could also pose a problem, as they make it more expensive for clients to raise the debt capital needed to purchase large volumes of chips. There is also the risk that demand on the customer-facing side of the AI industry will not be sufficient to justify the substantial spending on AI infrastructure.

    While Nvidia's recent dip might make the stock look like a tempting buy right now, the risks seem to outweigh the rewards. The recent scandal could expose Nvidia to heightened regulatory scrutiny of its business in Asia. The loss of Huang's leadership could hurt the manufacturer in ways that are difficult to predict right now. Investors should stay on the sidelines until more information becomes available.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Ryan Vanzo – Nov 21, 2026 at 1:27PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Recent findings suggest that many of the world's most valuable companies today are artificial intelligence (AI) stocks. That's for good reason. The global AI opportunity is truly massive, and many AI hyperscalers are already quite profitable. But what will happen to these companies during a market crash?

    Sources indicate that only around 10% of the S&P 500's value is tied directly to companies engaged in developing AI software. However, between 40% and 50% of the index's value is indirectly exposed to AI. That includes major GPU producers such as Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%), as well as AI-enabled software providers like Palo Alto Networks and ServiceNow.

    According to recent reports, in short, if markets fall, there's a very strong chance AI stocks will lead the way. It would be no surprise to see AI stocks struggle in a market downturn. While high growth rates may support premium valuations, companies with high growth rates already priced into shares typically falter as markets rerate risk tolerances. But as a recent report from BlackRock points out:.

    If market sentiment becomes risk-averse, pressuring AI stock valuations, investors would be wise to peruse the bargain bin for deals. There's one AI stock I'm keeping a very close eye on, as its underlying fundamentals and already cheap valuation should make it a strong buy during a market crash.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    During market crashes or economic downturns, companies with strong fundamentals often have an opportunity to grow stronger. That's because weaker competitors may face financial difficulties and exit the market. Acquisition prices get cheaper, with expansion opportunities facing less competition.

    According to recent reports, when conducting a meta-analysis of firms entering a downturn with strong financials and end-market demand, McKinsey & Co. found that these businesses "emerged much stronger coming out of the downturn, and the advantage they gained lasted for a long period.".

    Industry observers note that with this in mind, it's not hard to see Nvidia as a strong choice -- perhaps the strongest choice -- for investors during a market downturn. There is no denying that Nvidia's core business is exposed to long-term growth tailwinds. Both sales and earnings are presently growing at roughly 100% year over year. Growth rates should reach 50% to 100% annually over the coming years.

    Recent findings suggest that GPUs are critical components for the AI revolution. Even if Nvidia's leadership position weakens, resulting in lower market shares and compressed margins, top-line growth should remain in the double digits throughout the rest of the decade, perhaps even longer.

    Recent headwinds, however -- including an abrupt and controversial CEO transition, potential regulatory pressures, and allegations of circular financing -- have pushed Nvidia's price-to-earnings ratio down to just 16.2, with a forward price-to-earnings ratio of just 9.6.

    According to recent reports, nvidia generated $43 billion in free cash flow last quarter. And the company currently has $227 billion remaining on an upscaled share repurchase initiative.

    Recent findings suggest that despite near-term concerns, Nvidia remains a financial powerhouse that manufactures critical components essential to the AI industry's expansion. In the event of a downturn, the manufacturer can repurchase shares at a discount, reinvest heavily in research and development, and acquire competitors at bargain prices.

    It has been revealed that it's not clear how much cheaper Nvidia shares can get from here. The manufacturer's current fundamentals and near-term growth forecasts already make shares a buy. If a marketwide downturn hits, however, many longer-term concerns, such as eventual margin compression, may become fully priced into shares.

    In a recent development, there's still a lot we don't know about Nvidia's future, especially in today's environment. But what we do know is that the tech giant is completely self-funded; benefits from strong, secular growth tailwinds; and has the financial might to outinvest and perhaps even outright acquire much of its competition, barring the internal divisions of hyperscalers.

    I'm already strongly considering an investment in Nvidia. Oddly enough, a market downturn could actually strengthen that conviction.

    • James Harden played by far his best game in a Cleveland Cavaliers uniform on Friday night during NBA Cup group play.
    • The 37-year-old guard erupted for 51 points in a 128-119 home win over the Indiana Pacers, a season high and his most since joining the Cavaliers amid the 2025-26 campaign.
    • In a recent development, cleveland (9-8) improved to 2-1 in Cup competition, knocking on the Miami Heat's door atop East Group B.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    James Harden played by far his best game in a Cleveland Cavaliers uniform on Friday night during NBA Cup group play.

    The 37-year-old guard erupted for 51 points in a 128-119 home win over the Indiana Pacers, a season high and his most since joining the Cavaliers amid the 2025-26 campaign.

    In a recent development, cleveland (9-8) improved to 2-1 in Cup competition, knocking on the Miami Heat's door atop East Group B. Indiana (5-11), which trailed the Cavaliers by as many as 24 points, dropped to 1-2 in this year's NBA Cup.

    In a recent development, harden shot 15 of 26 from the floor, including 7 of 11 from beyond the arc. He also finished 14 of 14 from the charity stripe and with six rebounds and six assists. The one-time NBA MVP and 11-time All-Star now has the third-most 50-plus-point games in NBA history. With 26 such performances, he passed the late Kobe Bryant (25) on Friday and now trails Michael Jordan (31) and Wilt Chamberlain (118) in that category.

    While collecting his first 50-piece with the Cavaliers, Harden moved into ninth all-time for most combined NBA regular and postseason points. His handles were on full display. He rained down 3s, and he made an impact at the rim.

    Toronto came into Friday missing a trio of starters and on a six-game losing streak. Darko Rajaković's team was playing without RJ Barrett, Collin Murray-Boyles and, of course, Kawhi Leonard, who's still working his way back from a knee injury.

    And yet, the shorthanded Raptors (6-10) found a way on the road versus the Detroit Pistons (10-5) in NBA Cup action, ending their skid with a riveting 105-102 win.

    It's notable to note that Detroit isn't at full strength, either. Jalen Duren remains sidelined with a hamstring problem. Plus, Duncan Robinson is out with a quad strain.

    The absence of some star power didn't diminish what turned out to be an incredible matchup between two squads in East Group A and between a pair of former Montverde Academy teammates. Toronto's Scottie Barnes and Detroit's Cade Cunningham went toe-to-toe, particularly down the stretch.

    In a recent development, cunningham, who clocked out with 23 points and nine assists, hit a go-ahead 3-pointer over Barnes with less than 20 seconds remaining. Then, with the Raptors down one point, Barnes drove on Cunningham and reclaimed the lead.

    Cunningham tried to answer back but ended up with nowhere to go with the ball after picking up his dribble en route to the basket. He passed it, and Toronto rookie Allen Graves nabbed a steal that helped wrap up the victory.

    According to recent reports, barnes had 29 points, 5 rebounds and 5 assists. Graves, a first-round pick from Santa Clara making his first career start, piled up 20 points, 10 rebounds and 3 steals.

    According to recent reports, after that nail-biter, Toronto is 2-1 in East Group A, whereas Detroit is 1-1. The bottom dweller of the group, the Milwaukee Bucks (0-2 in NBA Cup play), was eliminated from knockout-round contention because the Raptors and Orlando Magic both won on Friday.

    The Magic left Brooklyn victorious 113-111, thanks to Franz Wagner, who scored 35 points on 13-of-25 shooting and knocked down a game-winning jumper with 2.4 ticks left against the Nets.

    Orlando is 3-0 in NBA Cup games this year.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    The neocloud had to delay the delivery of some new capacity due to challenges with a third-party provider. That wasn’t Nebius' fault, and the manufacturer is building its future data centers to avoid third-party risk moving forward. The end result is that Nebius claims it will not hit the $7 billion annual recurring revenue (ARR) target it forecast for December until February.

    In a recent development, anyone who is holding Nebius stock is doing so for the long run. While this two-month delay ruined short-term call options, it didn't affect the long-term thesis much. Artificial intelligence is still heating up, with demand scaling upward.

    Financing and profitability have been among the main concerns people have about the neocloud, but Nebius squashed them both in its third-quarter shareholder letter. Its latest contracts provide prepayments that cover all capital expenditures. Furthermore, the company expects to be breaking even on a pre-tax basis by 2027.

    According to recent reports, within five to 10 years, it's possible that the conversation will shift from Nebius raising money to management initiating stock buybacks. It's quite feasible, since the firm's payback period for newly introduced data centers has dropped to one year and seven months, and that excludes prepayments.

    Its annual contract value per megawatt now exceeds $25 million for long-term deals, and Nebius wasted no time mentioning key enterprise AI leaders that recently became new customers.

    Recent findings suggest that nebius believes it can generate $12 billion to $13 billion in ARR by the end of 2027. Granted, unforeseen delays could push some of that revenue out into 2028, as investors witnessed when Nebius said it wouldn’t reach its $7 billion ARR target until February.

    According to recent reports, importantly, though, that guidance reveals that growth is not slowing down. In Q3, Nebius delivered 571% year-over-year revenue growth to $981 million. That was also a 68% sequential growth rate from the second quarter.

    Recent findings suggest that nebius has said that it expects to be operating at breakeven on a pre-tax basis by the end of 2027, and that its data centers are recouping the capital investments required to bring them online in just 19 months. However, that's still underselling Nebius as an investment.

    It has been revealed that one key detail investors may be overlooking is how negotiations will change when it's time to renew contracts. Nebius has to negotiate prepayments to fund its data centers. Receiving capital up front makes it more viable to build data centers at scale.

    Sources indicate that customers make prepayments in exchange for lower annual contract values for each megawatt. Once Nebius operates data centers that have been fully paid off, it won't be as reliant on prepayments. That will give Nebius the flexibility to set higher prices per megawatt, and the soaring demand for compute implies that the elevated prices will stick.

    Nebius revealed in its Q2 shareholder letter that it gets annual contract values of $40 million to $50 million per megawatt for short-term deals. Customers aren't afraid of those prices, and long-term deals may get closer to those levels once prepayments are no longer necessary.

    Recent findings suggest that this detail, combined with Nebius' current performance and pipeline, suggests it can produce 100% or higher year-over-year revenue growth for multiple years. That's a pretty ambitious prediction, but Nebius has been delivering on that minimum growth rate in recent quarters. Guidance implies that ARR will roughly quadruple in a single year.

    #39354. Breaking: The S&P 500 Heads Into Thanksgiving Below Its Peak. Here's How the Holiday Week Has Usually Gone Since 1950.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (858 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: The S&P 500 Heads Into Thanksgiving Below Its Peak. Here's How the Holiday Week Has Usually Gone Since 1950.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (858 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) finished on Nov.
    • Chipmakers were among the worst hit that day, amid worries that the midterm election results might slow the artificial intelligence (AI) build-out.
    • It has been revealed that the market is closed on Thursday, Nov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 21, 2026 at 1:47PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    The S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) finished on Nov. 16 at 7,416.59, around 5% under the all-time closing high of 7,818.93 it set on Oct. 6. The drop sped up in late October, and the index fell over 4% on Nov. 5 alone as tech stocks sold off.

    Chipmakers were among the worst hit that day, amid worries that the midterm election results might slow the artificial intelligence (AI) build-out.

    It has been revealed that the market is closed on Thursday, Nov. 26, for Thanksgiving, and it closes early (at 1 p.m. ET) the next day.

    According to recent reports, historically, this has been a better-than-average week to hold stocks. Since 1950, the index has climbed during Thanksgiving week in 53 of 76 years, or about 70% of the time, and the week's average gain has been roughly 0.7%. By comparison, normal weeks across the same stretch rose 56% of the time and gained roughly 0.2% on average.

    But the record looks weaker in years like this one. In the 13 years the index entered the week 3% to 10% under a recent record close, it rose in just seven.

    I measured each year from the close on the Friday before Thanksgiving to the close on the Friday after, with the index's daily closes from Yahoo Finance (which count price moves only, not dividends). That normally includes four trading sessions around the holiday.

    Notably, the gains haven't been spread evenly among them. Monday and Tuesday combined averaged a gain of only about 0.1% and finished up in 47 of the 76 years. The Wednesday before Thanksgiving, though, climbed in 58 years and averaged a gain of around 0.3%. The Friday after climbed in 54, with an average gain close to that.

    So, the two sessions on either side of the holiday make up almost all the week's typical gain.

    Industry observers note that the range has been wide, too. The best Thanksgiving week came in 2008, in the middle of the financial crisis, when the index jumped about 12% from around half its record. The worst was 2011, with a loss of nearly 5%.

    It has been revealed that to match this year's setup, I looked for weeks that began with the index at least 3% but no more than 10% below its record close, with that record set within around four months. Thirteen years qualified, from 1951 to 2025.

    The week rose in seven of them, and the average gain was around 0.4%. That's still a little better than a regular week. But it's around half the average for all 76 Thanksgiving weeks, and the hit rate drops from about 70% to about 54%.

    The two latest cases went in opposite directions. In 2018, the index began the week around 7% below its September record and dropped nearly 4% more -- and by Dec. 31, it was about 8% below where it started the week.

    Industry observers note that last year, it came in about 4% under its Oct. 28 record and climbed nearly 4%.

    Also, the rest of the year was better for the group. In 10 of these 13 years, the index closed the year above its level on the Friday before Thanksgiving. Out of all 76 years, the same was true for 54.

    For anyone owning an S&P 500 index fund like the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -3.42%), the next 12 months may matter more than the next four sessions. Twelve of the 13 cases have a full year of data after them, and a year after the Friday before Thanksgiving, the index was up in six and down in six.

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    These years ranged from a rise of around 24% after 1963 to a drop of about 40% after 2007.

    It has been revealed that in 2007, the holiday week cost the index only about 1%. But the October record turned out to be the peak before a bear market that cut the index by over half. And 2018's bad week came before a rise of 14% over the next year.

    Sure, 13 years is a small sample, and the fall from a 70% hit rate to 54% could easily be chance.

    Sources indicate that the Vanguard fund finished Nov. 16 around $680, about 5% under the $718.47 peak it hit within the last year.

    I think the holiday week's history is a slight edge in investors' favor, and one that has mostly faded in years when the index started below a record. For a long-term owner of the fund, that isn't much to act on either way.

    Sources indicate that gable: "Biggest spread on the board right now. We opened at Bills -17, down to -16.5. Total has dropped two points, from 47 down to 45. Buffalo is in a ton of money-line parlays as you'd expect — the Bills and the Chiefs are two legs of many parlays. It's actually pretty balanced action on the spread.".

    Vikings vs. 49ers (in Mexico City).

    Recent findings suggest that feazel: "Really prolific 49ers offense versus very stingy Vikings defense. Even against the Packers last week, we haven't seen public gravitate towards Minnesota. We saw 49ers put up 46 points against Cowboys, but allowed 40. Likely going to need the Vikings here. It'll be all over money and a lot of 49ers money, as we approach Sunday night.".

    Gable: "We opened 49ers -3.5, quickly went to -3. Total sitting around 46 or 46.5, not much movement there. This game is interesting for a number of different reasons.     It has been revealed that feazel: "Second-biggest total on the board at 54.5. As you'd expect, Bengals money and the over. Don't blame anyone for that, it's been easy money to back that.     General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Better Buy: Bitcoin vs. Ethereum

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (750 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that bitcoin (BTC +3.05%) and Ether (ETH +3.40%) are the world's two most valuable cryptocurrencies.
    • Bitcoin, which reached $126,000 last October, is now worth roughly $60,000.
    • In the past, Bitcoin and Ether were both mined using the energy-intensive proof-of-work (PoW) consensus mechanism, in which miners used powerful computing hardware to solve cryptographic puzzles and earn tokens as rewards.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Leo Sun – Nov 21, 2026 at 1:55PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Bitcoin ›.

    It has been revealed that bitcoin (BTC +3.05%) and Ether (ETH +3.40%) are the world's two most valuable cryptocurrencies. But after setting record highs in 2025, both tokens tumbled in 2026.

    Bitcoin, which reached $126,000 last October, is now worth roughly $60,000. Ether, which topped $4,950 last August, trades at about $1,700. Let's see why these top "blue chip" cryptocurrencies crumbled -- and if either one is worth buying in this choppy market.

    In the past, Bitcoin and Ether were both mined using the energy-intensive proof-of-work (PoW) consensus mechanism, in which miners used powerful computing hardware to solve cryptographic puzzles and earn tokens as rewards.

    CRYPTO · As of 1:50 PM ET 11/21/26.

    But there was a key difference: Bitcoin was primarily designed as a digital commodity, while Ethereum (the blockchain behind Ether) was built to support complex smart contracts, which are used to develop decentralized apps and tokenized assets. Bitcoin supported only simple smart contracts, and its limited programmability made it less attractive to developers.

    According to recent reports, in 2022, the Ethereum network -- whose native token is Ether -- transitioned to the more energy-efficient proof-of-stake (PoS) consensus mechanism. Under PoS, validators stake (lock up) their Ether tokens to help secure the network and validate transactions, earning rewards for their participation rather than simply mining newly introduced tokens. The bigger Ethereum's developer ecosystem grows, the more valuable Ether -- which funds the "gas fees" for those transactions -- becomes.

    CRYPTO · As of 1:43 PM ET 11/21/26.

    Recent findings suggest that today, Ether's value is closely tied to Ethereum's developer growth, while Bitcoin's value is still driven by its scarcity, utility, and value to institutional investors. Bitcoin has a maximum supply of 21 million tokens. More than 20 million of those tokens have already been mined, and its blockchain undergoes a "halving" every four years to cut its mining rewards in half.

    It has been revealed that ether doesn't have a fixed maximum supply, and it fluctuates between being an inflationary token and a deflationary one based on Ethereum's network activity. Ethereum is upgrading its network to make it more scalable and secure, but it also faces intense competition from faster PoS blockchains like Solana (SOL +2.91%) and Cardano (ADA +3.68%). To stay ahead of these competitors, Ethereum is supporting more Layer 2 (L2) applications that bundle together transactions and process them off-chain at higher speeds than its Layer 1 (L1) blockchain.

    Bitcoin and Ether have more long-term catalysts than many other smaller altcoins, but they aren't immune to the macro headwinds for the broader crypto market. Last year, many crypto investors expected interest rate cuts, clearer, crypto-friendly regulations, and lower Treasury yields to drive investors back toward cryptocurrencies and riskier investments.

    But the opposite happened. The Iran war exacerbated inflation, driving the Fed to raise its rates for the first time in three years. Treasury yields spiked, and the CLARITY Act -- which would have provided a clearer regulatory framework for cryptocurrencies -- died in the Senate.

    In a recent development, the Democratic sweep of the U.S. midterm elections also suggests that more restrictive regulations could be passed against the crypto industry. All of those challenges chilled the crypto market and drove investors toward safer, higher-yielding investments again.

    In a recent development, bitcoin and Ether will both remain under pressure for the foreseeable future. But if I had to pick one over the other, I'd buy Bitcoin because it has more growth potential as a hedge against expansionary monetary policies and the debasement of fiat currencies. Once its price stabilizes, it could become more comparable to "digital gold" than other cryptocurrencies.

    Sources indicate that ether also has a bright future as the "digital oil" of decentralized applications. Still, that future is murkier due to intense competition from Solana, Cardano, and other PoS blockchains with faster transactions and lower fees. Unless Ether widens its moat against those competitors, it could have less upside potential than Bitcoin when the crypto winter finally ends.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Recent findings suggest that viper Energy (VNOM) is a subsidiary of Diamondback and owns and acquires mineral and royalty interests, primarily in the Permian Basin. The manufacturer reported upbeat third-quarter earnings, supported by recent acquisitions and continued development activity from Diamondback and third-party operators. Viper announced a base cash dividend of 50 cents per share for Q3 2026, payable on Nov. 19. Based on the base and variable dividends announced over the past 12 months, VNOM's dividend yield stands at 5.7%.

    Following the Q3 results, TD Cowen analyst Aaron Bilkoski reiterated a buy rating on Viper Energy stock with a price target of $61. The analyst noted that the firm delivered solid Q3 results, with production, including oil and natural gas liquids, exceeding both TD Cowen and consensus estimates.

    The 5-star analyst highlighted that the key patch was the announcement of two royalty acquisitions for $809 million in cash, including deferred consideration, and $82 million of newly issued shares.

    It has been revealed that given the recently confirmed base dividend hike, Bilkoski expects Viper to direct incremental free cash flow toward buybacks. While the acquisitions increase leverage, the analyst believes that Viper has enough capacity for opportunistic buybacks.

    In a recent development, bilkoski noted that Viper has historically delivered one of the highest production per share growth profiles in his royalty coverage, but still trades at a notable discount to the royalty peer average and the company's historical FCF yield range. "In our view, its above-average growth warrants a higher valuation," said the analyst.

    Industry observers note that bilkoski ranks No. 525 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.80%. See Viper Energy Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

    Industry observers note that exxon Mobil (XOM) reported robust Q3 2026 profits, as its U.S. refineries boosted production to capitalize on the high diesel fuel prices sparked by the conflict in the Middle East. The oil and gas giant announced a quarterly dividend of $1.07 per share, payable on Dec. 10, reflecting a 3.9% increase. This marks Exxon's 44th consecutive year of dividend increases. At an annualized dividend of $4.28 per share, XOM offers a yield of 2.53%.

    Impressed by the Q3 print, TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Exxon stock and raised his price target to $193 from $180 to reflect higher downstream earnings, with the expectation of increased mid-cycle margins.

    Sources indicate that gabelman noted that the strength in Exxon's refining business continues to offset Middle East-related headwinds. He added that the firm increased its ownership in LNG projects, which should reduce its Middle East concentration over time from 75% to 50% and lower the likelihood of diversification-focused mergers and acquisitions. Beyond LNG, Gabelman expects Exxon's growth in the 2030s to come from Guyana, Kashagan, Permian, and possibly Venezuela.

    It has been revealed that gabelman noted that Exxon revealed a dividend hike of nearly 4% and aims to maintain buybacks at $20 billion for 2027. "The decision to maintain reduces the pro-cyclicality nature of the buyback," remarked the analyst.

    In a recent development, gabelman ranks No. 347 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.90%. See Exxon Mobil Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Williams (WMB), which owns and operates energy infrastructure to deliver natural gas, reported strong third-quarter results. The company announced a quarterly dividend of $0.525 per share, or $2.10 per share annualized, payable on Dec. 28. WMB offers a dividend yield of 3.09%.

    In reaction to the Q3 2026 results, CIBC analyst Robert Catellier reaffirmed a buy rating on Williams stock with a price target of $82. The analyst noted that Q3 results were essentially in line with expectations and reflected continued strength in execution across WMB's infrastructure portfolio.

    Catellier remarked that Williams' Q3 performance was driven by higher transmission, storage, and power generation revenues, as well as contributions from the Momentum Midstream acquisition.

    He noted that Williams maintained its full-year EBITDA guidance of $8.3 billion to $8.5 billion. In fact, results are tracking toward the higher end of the guidance range, backed by contributions from recently completed projects and the Momentum Midstream deal. WMB continues to target long-term EBITDA compound annual growth rate of at least 11% through 2030.

    Catellier expects WMB's long-term targets to be supported by incremental transmission and storage opportunities, including Transco's Southeast Supply Enhancement II project and an 84 MMcf/d expansion of the Garden Connector project.

    Tokenization platform Securitize gains 10% postmarket on Q3 results, move into asset-backed finance

    📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (443 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.
    • According to recent reports, miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively newly introduced corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure.
    • The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    According to recent reports, miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively newly introduced corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the tech giant like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The company posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    Industry observers note that also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and declared the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo said.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

    #39321. Breaking: What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (741 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (741 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the firm's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
    • Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the organization.
    • Nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the firm's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

    Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the organization. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

    Nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

    "Although we expect the tech giant to fulfill all of its previously announced commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate upcoming multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said in a note Thursday.

    The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

    According to recent reports, tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

    On Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    Tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

    Recent findings suggest that it's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The tech giant had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

    Neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

    CoreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

    It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, remarked CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

    "We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he mentioned.

    "However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

    CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

    According to recent reports, "There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my tech giant every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he mentioned in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

    Bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any big changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

    The real issue is just how much money the company will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

    Recent findings suggest that "Major companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he stated. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

    — CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

    #39295. Is a bottom in for the Nasdaq-100? Charts to watch

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (580 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Is a bottom in for the Nasdaq-100? Charts to watch

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (580 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).
    • Recent findings suggest that is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in?
    • First, let's remember how we got here.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).

    Recent findings suggest that is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in? We're going to look at several charts to help answer that question.

    First, let's remember how we got here. In September, the NDX broke out from a bullish cup-and-handle pattern, producing a 33,200-upside target. That breakout promptly failed, however, and gave way to a bearish pattern that broke down aggressively two weeks ago.

    The decline brought the index relatively close to its 26,350 downside target before the current rebound began.

    In a recent development, zooming out, it's telling to see where the bounce originated. Three important forms of support converged in the 25,000-26,000 area:.

    This confluence of support helped encourage buying after a roughly 15% decline.

    For perspective, we also see what larger drawdowns of 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% would look like … a lot worse.

    The following chart tracks NDX drawdowns from 52-week highs going back to just after the financial crisis. Only a handful of declines exceeded 20%, and three produced relatively quick reversals: late 2018, the Covid lows in 2020 and April 2025.

    Historically, buying into declines of approximately 15%–25% has generally paid off, even when additional downside occurred first (yellow highlights).

    The chart also highlights previous declines of 10%–16% in green, putting the current pullback into perspective.

    The major exception was 2022, when the NDX eventually declined nearly 36% over approximately 10 months ... a much worse outcome, which many investors are concerned could happen again now.

    That raises the key question: Are we experiencing another routine correction, or the early stages of a larger bear market?

    One crucial clue will be how far this bounce progresses.

    According to recent reports, any rally that fails to reclaim the previous highs could establish a significant lower high. Additional lower highs would provide stronger evidence of a developing, longer downtrend.

    We saw this in March 2022, when that first sharp rebound effort failed to reach the previous high before a much more severe decline followed.

    The bottom line: The current bounce is encouraging, particularly given where it originated and knowing how well buying prior 10-20% drawdowns has paid off.

    From here, it's all about the follow through. We don't need to see newly introduced highs right away, but any rally from here that's met with another wave of strong selling could reignite downside momentum.

    #39275. Industry News: A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (626 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (626 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct.
    • According to recent reports, however, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive.
    • Recent findings suggest that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct. 6. The market despises uncertainty, and losing a visionary founder, particularly one without a well-telegraphed succession plan, makes it worse.

    According to recent reports, however, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive. Trading in the $160s, Nvidia's valuation has taken a significant haircut, yet its underlying business fundamentals remain largely intact. While Huang was the architect of Nvidia's AI dominance, the tech giant's moat — superior GPUs, the CUDA software ecosystem, and networking expertise — does not walk out the door with him. The company's structural advantage in the global artificial intelligence rollout persists.

    Recent findings suggest that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options. Huang's departure guarantees that Nvidia will be operating under a cloud of transition for the foreseeable future. Executing a permanent CEO search while navigating global regulatory scrutiny takes time. Consequently, Nvidia's implied volatility (IV)—the market's pricing of expected future price swings — has spiked to highs not seen since the tariff tantrum in the first half of 2025, and this elevated IV is highly likely to persist for several months as the leadership drama slowly unfolds.

    This prolonged period of high implied volatility can be a goldmine for option sellers, specifically those executing options overlays such as covered call strategies. When you buy NVDA shares at these depressed levels and simultaneously sell out-of-the-money call options against your position, the premiums you collect are directly tied to IV. Because fear and transition-related uncertainty have dramatically inflated these option prices, the income generated from selling covered calls is now significantly higher than usual.

    It has been revealed that this lowers the risk profile of holding the stock considerably over time. Consistently collecting these inflated premiums systematically lowers your overall cost basis in the underlying shares. If the stock trades sideways or recovers slowly during the CEO search, you are generating an outsized cash yield on a stagnant asset. If the stock experiences further downside turbulence, the heavy premium income acts as a substantial downside buffer, meaningfully reducing the strategy's overall risk over time.

    By deploying a persistent covered call strategy, investors can leverage the exact fear driving the stock down to generate robust, risk-reducing income while maintaining exposure to the undeniable future of AI.

    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Anthropic raises $93.5 billion total as underwriters scoop up ‘greenshoe’ overallotment

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (417 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic underwriters have officially exercised their overallotment of shares in the historic initial public offering, bringing the total raised to $93.5 billion, according to a release Friday.
    • The artificial intelligence company raised $81.3 billion on Wednesday and netted an additional $12.2 billion through the overallotment, surpassing SpaceX, which held a record IPO in June.
    • Recent findings suggest that anthropic said it sold an aggregate of 1,127,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock at $83 per share in the offering.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Anthropic underwriters have officially exercised their overallotment of shares in the historic initial public offering, bringing the total raised to $93.5 billion, according to a release Friday.

    The artificial intelligence company raised $81.3 billion on Wednesday and netted an additional $12.2 billion through the overallotment, surpassing SpaceX, which held a record IPO in June.

    Recent findings suggest that anthropic said it sold an aggregate of 1,127,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock at $83 per share in the offering. It sold 980 million shares on Wednesday and its underwriters had the option to purchase up to an additional 147 million shares by Friday as part of the overallotment, which is commonly referred to as the "greenshoe.".

    Shares of the Claude maker opened trading at $111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday, but slid throughout the day and closed at $97.17. The stock sank 12% in premarket trading on Friday during a broad tech sell-off.

    Recent findings suggest that in addition to the sale of its Class A common stock, Anthropic closed a concurrent sale of its Class N common stock after a group of tech companies, including Advanced Micro Devices, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and others, agreed to participate in a $26 billion private placement at the IPO price. Anthropic said Friday that aggregate gross proceeds from its IPO, including the private placement, totaled $119.5 billion, before deducting offering expenses.

    Anthropic dodged an unforgiving series of obstacles on its road to the Nasdaq on Thursday, as investors brooded over Jensen Huang's shocking ouster at Nvidia, voters' stinging rebuke of the tech during the midterms and whether rising interest rates would stymie industry aims for a multitrillion-dollar AI infrastructure buildout.

    CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after he and a handful of other researchers, including his sister Daniela, quit their jobs at OpenAI, now Anthropic's chief rival. Anthropic is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude, which have captivated the corporate world and fueled the company's historic rise.

    The siblings celebrated the IPO as a "milestone" in an interview with CNBC on Thursday, but said there's more work ahead for Anthropic.

    It has been revealed that "For us, it's like one stop on the journey," Daniela Amodei said. "We think about this as, 'Wow, this is an incredible moment for Anthropic for our mission, but we're going to wake up tomorrow and we're going to be the same organization.'".

    #39260. Trump indicates he discussed Jensen Huang with Xi; Bessent tells CNBC Nvidia chip export policy is unchanged

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (870 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Trump indicates he discussed Jensen Huang with Xi; Bessent tells CNBC Nvidia chip export policy is unchanged

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (870 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, president Donald Trump on Friday mentioned he and Chinese leader Xi Jinping discussed their shared affinity for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during their talks in China this week.
    • "I did discuss that with President Xi, and he stated, 'Oh, brilliant, brilliant!
    • Asked earlier Friday on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" if Huang, a close ally of Trump's, had come up in "any of your discussions with the Chinese," Bessent noted "no," without elaborating.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, president Donald Trump on Friday mentioned he and Chinese leader Xi Jinping discussed their shared affinity for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during their talks in China this week. Earlier in the day, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the ousted leader was not mentioned in separate talks he had with Chinese officials.

    "I did discuss that with President Xi, and he stated, 'Oh, brilliant, brilliant! He's a brilliant man.' He is," Trump said at a White House press conference.

    Asked earlier Friday on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" if Huang, a close ally of Trump's, had come up in "any of your discussions with the Chinese," Bessent noted "no," without elaborating.

    A senior Trump administration official later said that both Trump's and Bessent's remarks were correct, and that both were addressing their own conversations. The official spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss those conversations.

    Trump also reiterated that he would like to see Huang — who was replaced by interim CEO Colette Kress after resigning amid allegations of an extramarital affair with a Chinese spy — be restored as Nvidia's CEO.

    "I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance," Trump stated. "You know, we're a country of second chances, and I'd love to be able to see him. That's a very notable firm to us, and he put us in a position where we are literally 10 years advanced over other companies.".

    Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Huang back, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC earlier this week.

    In a recent development, the president's comments came amid growing scrutiny of advanced U.S. chips, including those made by Nvidia, ending up in China either legally or by being diverted via third countries.

    Both Trump's and Bessent's remarks are potentially an indication that the Trump administration may not focus on cracking down on China's efforts to acquire advanced chips.

    In a recent development, bessent suggested that U.S. policy allowing the sale of Nvidia's powerful H200 AI chips to China remains unchanged following the talks in Shenzhen this week.

    "We've already agreed that the ... H200s are the threshold level of chips that could be sold to the Chinese, and, you know, that continues as planned," Bessent said.

    "I wouldn't anticipate any change in the policy," he added after CNBC's Sara Eisen noted that Nvidia remarked it had stopped selling H200s to China.

    Sources indicate that the administration ignoring the subject of Huang's affair with a possible Chinese spy — whose Singapore-based firm Megaspeed has been accused of acting as a cutout for Beijing — contrasts with the importance Trump has placed on beating China in the race to artificial intelligence dominance. It could suggest that despite his support for the U.S. AI industry, Trump is less concerned with addressing China's ongoing efforts to acquire U.S. semiconductors.

    Trump has also defended Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who has come under fire from multiple directions for reportedly slow-walking export restrictions on Chinese chip sales. "I understand both sides of it," Trump said on Monday when he also said he's like to see Huang back as CEO.

    Bessent's appearance on CNBC came after Trump's return from a tour through Asia that saw him meet with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China.

    The meeting was historic as the first time the leaders of the three countries had met without other nations' counterparts. But the trilateral summit appeared to yield few deliverables on any number of the most pressing global issues related to the countries, including the Ukraine and Iran wars or the ongoing AI race.

    Bessent told CNBC on Friday that there was a "robust discussion" between Trump and Xi on trade policy and AI.

    They "agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions," he noted, abbreviating the term "super intelligence," Trump's attempted rebrand of AI.

    In a CNBC appearance last week, Bessent lamented the "leakage" of U.S.-made AI chips to China and blamed the Commerce Department, led by Lutnick, for slow-walking export controls on suspected Chinese cutouts like Megaspeed.

    Multiple Trump administration leaders have long sought to impose export restrictions on Megaspeed, but Commerce "has the pen" and "you will have to ask them about their internal processes," Bessent noted in that interview.

    On Friday, however, Bessent was much more tight-lipped.

    Recent findings suggest that asked if there is a dispute between him and Lutnick over how aggressively the U.S. should be pursuing Chinese export controls, Bessent said, "I think we're all committed to following President Trump's instructions.".

    "I think we are going to see that the ... proper chip restrictions are in place, and the remote access has been curtailed," he added. Commerce recently took steps to close one of China's paths to accessing AI processors.

    Correction: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent spoke to CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." A previous version of this story misstated the name of the show.

    Editor's note: This story and headline have been updated following additional information provided by the Trump administration about the nature of Bessent's and Trump's meetings in China.
